thread:
maria-p: quick check — i'm prototyping an auto-tune pipeline to surface adaptive SLO thresholds in the console. goal: keep thresholds tight to catch regressions but avoid noisy notify fanout. tentative formula: derived = ewma(p95, 24h) + alpha * rolling_std(p95, 24h). thoughts? :thinking:

jonas-k: overall ok as a heuristic. couple operational concerns: 1) low-traffic tenants will have flaky std, 2) simultaneous threshold flips across tenants could spike notify, 3) need a clear fallback when samples < min_samples.

tara: agree. propose these mitigations: min_samples gate (fallback to org-default), absolute cap on delta (max_delta_ms), hysteresis windows before commit, and a "routing_influence" knob to bias how much derived impacts notify routing.

maria-p: sketching knobs: min_samples=50, max_delta_pct=30, max_delta_ms=250, alpha=1.2, hysteresis=2 windows, ewma_alpha=0.15, routing_influence=0.4. also thinking about a "staging_mode" where proposed thresholds are computed and logged but not applied.

jonas-k: +1. for staging we should run a shadow mode for 72h and emit metrics: proposed_threshold_ts, delta_vs_current, predicted_notify_fanout. that lets us estimate volume impact without touching routing.

slo-bot: scheduled shadow-run autotune-shadow-2026-03 cohort=5% start=1736009000 duration=72h. output prefix: /telemetry/autotune/shadow/autotune-shadow-2026-03

maria-p: rollout plan idea: 1) shadow (no routing) 72h, 2) limited canary (5% tenants) with routing_influence=0.8 (i.e., 20% effective weight), 3) increase weight gradually if alert delta < 5% and no regression alerts. emergency stop via console toggle.

jonas-k: add notify_service_backpressure config: if notify_queue_depth > X or error_rate > Y, pause applying any derived thresholds. also add a per-org opt-out flag surfaced in console.

tara: telemetry dashboards we need: a) derived_threshold_time_series, b) percent_tenants_using_autotune, c) notify_fanout_delta_by_cohort, d) alerts_triggered_vs_baseline, e) fallback_count (when min_samples not met). create a synthetic signal generator to exercise edge cases.

maria-p: here's a compact YAML snippet for RFC:

```yaml
autotune:
  metric: p95_latency_ms
  baseline: ewma(24h)
  baseline_window: 24h
  ewma_alpha: 0.15
  alpha: 1.2
  min_samples: 50
  max_delta_pct: 30
  max_delta_ms: 250
  hysteresis_windows: 2
  routing_influence: 0.4  # 0 = none, 1 = full
  notify_backpressure_threshold:
    queue_depth: 1000
    error_rate_pct: 1.0
  staging_mode: true
  cohort_pct: 0.05
```

jonas-k: small nit: make min_samples default 100 for safety. also add "apply_mode" enum: [shadow, staged, live] so API is explicit. log an audit event on every derived threshold change.

tara: unit tests needed: constant series (std=0), nan handling, tiny sample counts, and spike injection to ensure hysteresis prevents flip-flop. also include integration test that asserts notify_fanout delta under threshold for canary cohort.

ops-bot: note: shadow-run autotune-shadow-2026-03 started at 1736009000. monitor dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/autotune-shadow-2026-03

maria-p: thanks. i'll update the RFC and add the dashboard panels and the synthetic signal harness. plan to run shadow 72h, then staged canary with routing_influence=0.8 for 24h, then evaluate. tagging @jonas-k @tara for review. :thumbsup:

jonas-k: +1

tara: +1, will review the RFC and tests later today.
